title: Prime Minister congratulates the nation on achieving 7.8% GDP growth; highlights surging economic confidence
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today congratulated the nation on achieving a Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth rate of 7.8% in the first quarter of the financial year. Sharing a video message, the Prime Minister highlighted the strong economic numbers, emphasizing that these figures reflect a surging economic confidence.
In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:
"7.8% growth.
Strong numbers.
Even stronger confidence."
7.8% growth. Strong numbers. Even stronger confidence. pic.twitter.com/ZVPpnAXrVU — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 1, 2026
***
MJPS/SS/PRK

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the nation after India recorded a GDP growth rate of 7.8% in the first quarter of the financial year. In a video message and a post on social media platform X, he described the figures as reflecting surging economic confidence, using the phrase 'Strong numbers. Even stronger confidence.'
enrichment.context: Quarterly GDP growth figures are released by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and are a key indicator tracked by policymakers, investors, and international agencies like the IMF and World Bank when assessing India's economic trajectory. A growth rate of 7.8% for Q1 would place India among the fastest-growing major economies, and such figures are often contextualised against previous quarters, the Reserve Bank of India's growth projections, and global economic headwinds such as inflation, geopolitical tensions, and trade disruptions. Q1 of the Indian financial year runs from April to June, and growth figures for this period are typically released by MoSPI around August-end. This particular release, however, is a brief celebratory statement by the Prime Minister rather than a detailed data release, and does not include sectoral breakdowns, comparisons with previous quarters, or methodological details, which are usually found in the official NSO press note.

prelims_questions.question: Which organisation is responsible for the official release of India's quarterly GDP growth estimates?
prelims_questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, compiles and releases India's quarterly and annual GDP growth estimates.

prelims_questions.question: In the Indian financial year, which months constitute the first quarter (Q1) for which GDP growth figures are typically reported?
prelims_questions.explanation: India's financial year runs from April to March, making April-June the first quarter (Q1), for which GDP data is usually released in late August.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of quarterly GDP growth data as an indicator of economic health. What are the limitations of using GDP growth rate alone to assess the well-being of an economy?

study_notes.reason: The release is a brief celebratory statement by the PM on Q1 GDP growth with no sectoral breakdown, comparative analysis, or policy detail; the only fact of note is the headline growth figure itself.

prelims.point: India's Q1 (April-June) FY2026-27 GDP growth rate was recorded at 7.8%, as per National Statistical Office (NSO) data under MoSPI.
prelims.why_important: Quarterly GDP figures and their releasing authority (NSO/MoSPI) are a recurring prelims fact-check area, especially when a notable growth rate is announced.

low_priority.point: PM's celebratory social media post describing the GDP figures as reflecting 'surging economic confidence'.
low_priority.reason: Political rhetoric without accompanying policy analysis, sectoral data, or comparative context; not examinable material.

related_articles.title: India's Index of industrial production records growth of 6.7% in July 2026.
related_articles.relationship: Both releases report on key macroeconomic indicators for the same period, with the IIP growth of 6.7% in July 2026 forming part of the broader economic momentum narrative that the PM's GDP growth statement builds on.
